# Data-management read

> Historical/rehearsal evidence notice (pre-2026-08-31): owner labels, route counts, and Go/retained statuses in this ledger describe the qualification snapshot at capture time, not current production ownership.
>
> Current route truth is derived from `node scripts/rust-migration/check-stage9-route-coverage.mjs` and `tests/fixtures/rust-migration/stage9/route-ownership.json`; formal release truth is `node scripts/rust-migration/check-stage9-closeout.mjs --check`. The original evidence below is intentionally retained verbatim.

- Group: `data-management-read`
- Tier: B: the GET projection inspects all managed SQLite files, rebuild
  markers, schema compatibility and storage metadata.
- Operation: `GET /api/v1/settings/data-management/databases`.
- Owner: Go remains the production owner. Rust opens existing database files
  read-only through the Stage 9 overview adapter and never initializes,
  migrates, repairs, compacts, backs up or cleans a database in this read
  slice.
- Frozen reference: the Go reference generated by
  `TestStage9DataManagementOverviewReference` and replayed by
  `stage9_data_management_overview_matches_current_go_owner` covers complete,
  summary, filtered and unknown-database cases over compatible, missing and
  incompatible SQLite states.

The authenticated sidecar rehearsal compares complete wire status/body/header
snapshots for the same query shapes, preserves injected Rust errors, fails
closed on timeout/crash, and switches to the Go-only router only after restart.
The authenticated Rust product test additionally proves that inspecting a
directory containing only `settings.json` creates no managed database, marker
or sidecar file and leaves the settings bytes unchanged.

Compatibility quirk: closing and reopening the Go owner checkpoints some WAL
files, so `mainBytes`, `walBytes`, `shmBytes`, `totalBytes`, `freePageBytes` and
`reclaimableBytes` can legitimately change across the restart boundary. The
live proxy comparison remains byte-exact; only the post-restart rollback
comparison normalizes those storage counters together with timestamps.

- Rust authenticated/read-only product route: `cargo test -p jftrade-engine --lib product::tests::data_management_read_tests::data_management_overview_is_authenticated_and_does_not_create_missing_databases -- --exact`.
- Go authenticated rehearsal: `go test ./internal/app/apiserver/servercoretest -run '^TestDataManagementReadRehearsalPreservesWireAndRequiresRestartForGoRollback$' -count=1`.
- Current route coverage: 1 shadow / 118 cutover-test-only / 159 cutover-qualified / 0 remaining / 0 Rust production owner.

The route is `cutover-qualified`, `productionOwner=go`, and
`goRemovalStatus=retained`. All data-management mutations remain
`cutover-test-only`; no default Rust write owner was enabled.
